title: Living on the West Coast and the Impulse Further Definitions albums
summary: He did not miss New York; Further Definitions recreated saxophone-section sounds with Hawkins, and no albums followed because nobody asked.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: ... all right, Benny, I want to continue with you now, summarizing this varied period of the 50's and 60's, which is so different from your career in the late 20's and the 30's and 40's. We tend to think in these decades, but of course, they overlap a bit.
Now you do, in the 50's, a variety of things, as I mentioned earlier, including records, albums with these

groups that you pick up for various purposes. They tend to be musicians more on the West Coast now than on the East Coast. There's a long period of time when you don't play on the East Coast, except later at the Newport Jazz Festivals, but for a long time, you're not appearing on the East Coast at all. Isn't that true?
Yes, that is quite true.
Uh huh. Did you miss New York?
Not really.
You liked it out there.
Yes, I liked living in California, and when I go to New York, it's always something I look forward to, and as soon as I get there, I'm ready to leave.
Certainly by the time you've finished, anyway.

Certainly, yes. I always say I'm gonna stay a few days, you know, longer, but I don't really have any real desire once I spend a little time there. I haven't spent much time playing there in the last few years, although I was there, I think, oh, a couple of times -- probably once in '62 and once in '65, just conducting the show for Peggy Lee.
Right.
... during which I didn't play at all, you know?
Right. It's around that time, too,
that you made one or two albums for Impulse, and for a long time after that, you didn't make an album. Those were the "Further Definitions" and "Additions to Further Definitions."
Right.
And in the first one, you -- what was the theme or the motif of the further definitions?
Well, as Bob Thiele
Field?

Field, mentioned to me -- he'd like me to, you know, just use the saxophone section and recreate a couple of things that Coleman Hawkins and I had done in Paris many years earlier with the two French saxophone players, Andre Ekyan, the altoist, and Alex Combelle, who is a tenor saxophone player; so we got together, oh, Phil Woods on the other alto and Charlie Rouse on the other tenor, Coleman Hawkins, myself -- with Jimmy Garrison on base and Dick Katz on piano, and Joe Jones on drums and John Collins on guitar, just with the 8 piece group, we made that "Further Definitions."
And you did a few of the tunes of those famous brase.
Yeah, "Crazy Rhythm" and "Honeysuckle Rose" ... and we did some other things.
Uh huh. Then you did an "Additions" to Further Definitions.
Yes.
And do you ... was there any special
reason why you didn't do any albums after the second of these two?
The only special reason was that nobody asked me! So I suppose that's good enough unless I wanted to so some myself, which I kept saying I was going to do, but never got around to it.
